author: Boombumi
quote:
A massive disappointment disguised as a video game.

After years of waiting, hype and marketing, GTA VI looks like a perfect example of how a franchise can lose its identity. From a world of freedom to a world of wokedom. We were sold the game of the century. The mere fact that opinions are so divided already tells us that it is nowhere near deserving that title.

The two protagonists are painfully uninteresting, with little personality or charisma. The dialogues feel uninspired, the writing lacks depth, and the story doesn't seem to offer anything particularly compelling. Having two playable characters means absolutely nothing when neither of them is worth caring about.

What bothers me most is the direction Rockstar has taken. GTA used to be a satirical, provocative and genuinely entertaining franchise. Now it feels increasingly focused on looking impressive rather than delivering an engaging experience. Better graphics and a bigger map don't automatically make a better game. There is no freedom, missions are still linear, and it's still FedEx gameplay...
Without repeating every other comment about how it's not a romance between the two characters, but rather a boss lady and her slave.

At this point, it feels less like playing Grand Theft Auto and more like being sold an expensive interactive simulator with a forgettable story attached to it, and a slave boyfriend simulator that does everything the boss lady wants him to.

I play a game for fun, not to do chores that I already do in real life.

Final verdict: 1/10.

A disappointing direction for one of gaming's most iconic franchises. All that waiting for something that, at least from what it offers, doesn't deserve the name GTA.
